newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB's 4.6% bond due Jan 98 traded at 7.2%--traders.
newsitem.headline: NCB's 4.6% bond due Jan 98 traded at 7.2%--traders.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd's 4.6 percent five-year debenture due January 1998 was traded at a yield of 7.2 percent on Tuesday morning in Tokyo, traders said.
About 200 million worth of the 4.6 percent debenture was traded this morning, they said.
The offer rate for any NCB debenture was quoted as high as seven percent on Monday.
The market yields of NCB debentures have been under upward pressure since Moody's Investors Service cut its rating for the bank's debentures last week.

Bank debentures came under additional selling pressure on Monday after a ruling party official said debentures bought by institutional investors should not be protected by public funds, bond traders said.
Moody's said on March 21 that it had cut the rating for NCB's debentures to Ba1 from Baa3.

Taku Yamasaki, chairman of the policy-making committee of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, said in a television programme on Sunday that bank debentures sold to institutional investors should not be protected by the use of public funds.
A 1.2 percent two-year NCB debenture due in August was traded at a yield of 6.7 percent this morning. The traded volume was about 200 million yen, traders said.
